message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "---
name: rpm-test

on:
  push:
    branches: [master]
  pull_request:
    branches: [master]
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  fedora:
    name: Check that Fedora RPM patches still apply
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - name: Check that Fedora patches apply
        run: for p in rpm/fedora/*.patch; do patch -p1 -s --fuzz=0 --no-backup-if-mismatch -f < "$p"; done
  centos:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    name: Check that CentOS RPM patches still apply
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - name: Check that CentOS patches apply
        run: for p in rpm/centos/*.patch; do patch -p1 -s --fuzz=0 --no-backup-if-mismatch -f < "$p"; done",
  "rationale": "The workflow runs two short patch-application jobs (fedora and centos) that only check out code and apply RPM patches. The P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT pattern (bound jobs with a custom timeout) is supported by measured evidence showing reduced runaway consumption with no loss of required checks. Repository CI history shows these jobs complete in seconds, so a 5-minute timeout provides safe operational headroom without affecting valid runs or coverage. No dependency installation occurs, so dependency caching patterns do not apply.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508", "experiment:batch-interactive-three--112e2b2e7fbe04b8"]
}
